Asad Hossain Chowdhury, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners. 
Kh. Saiful Hoque with Khalilur Rahman Rakani, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Saleha Khatun and others ------ Petitioners
vs
Fetema Hajura and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule issued on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the order dated 6-3-1991 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Additional Court Rajshahi in OC suit No. 402 of 1982/69 of 1990 allowing an application for amendment of the plaint by way of striking out the name of the deceased sole defendant and adding the names of his legal heirs of the deceased defendant in his place.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of this application, in short, is that predecessor-in-interest of the opposite parties as plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title in the suit land mentioned in the plaint being CC Suit No. 402 of 1982 in the court of Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi against late Khandaker Mafizuddin predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner as sole defendant.

3. The case of the plaintiff, inter alia, is that Ashutosh Roy was the CS recorded tenant of the suit land along with other land under the Ex-lord Abdul Hakim Chowdhury, Ashutosh Roy while in ownership and possession died leaving two sons Kalipada Roy and Devi Pada Roy whose names were recorded in SA Khatian. Thereafter said Kalipada and Devi Pada sold out the suit property along with others to plaintiff by registered sale deed dated 11-8-1969 and delivered possession. During Revisional settlement suit property has been wrongly recorded in the name of the defendant. The plaintiff came to know about wrong recording of the suit property in the name of the defendant from the local Tahasildar on 15-6-1982. It is stated that as a result the wrong record of RS. Khatian in the name of the defendant has been a cloud cast upon the title of the plaintiff and hence plaintiff filed the suit.

4. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegation. The case of the defendant, inter alia, is that the suit land comprising an area of 0.50 acre in CS plot No. 279 originally belonged to Rajkhear debuttar Estate of which two brothers named Kali Pada Roy and Devi Pada Roy were joint shebaits, that one Hazrat Ali took pattan of an area measuring .04½ acre from the Estate in the first part of the year 1360 BS at an annual Jama of Rs. 9/15/0, that said Hazrat Ali while in ownership and possession of the land on regular payment of rent to the landlord sold the pattan land to the defendant by registered sale deed dated 30-4-1954 at a consideration of Taka 97.00 Only. The said Hazrat Ali also sold the rest of the pattan land to the defendant by registered sale deed dated 3-11-1954 and thus defendant became owner and possessor of 0.5½  acre of land, that the defendant has been possessing the suit land openly, peacefully and adversely for more then 12 years by mutating his name and paying rent. At about the time of taking pattan by Hazrat Ali, one Anwara Khatun also took pattan of 0.04½  acres of land where she had homestead and she sold a portion out of her pattan land to one Shamsuddin and said vendor had possession of the land and as such, they were necessary parties in the suit, that the land purchased by the defendant was wrongly recorded in the SA Khatian in the name of Kalipada and Devi Pada and for correction of record the defendant filed Miscellaneous case which was decreed ex parte on 17-4-1970 and record of right was accordingly corrected. During RS operation the suit land has been correctly recorded in the name of the defendant. Against such record that plaintiff filed dispute and objection case before the settlement Authority which were rejected on 27-2-1973 and 10-4-1978 and as such, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation, that RS Khatian has been finally published in the name of the defendant, that plaintiff has illegally and fraudulently created some deeds in respect of the entire area of the land in suit plot, that as a matter of fact plaintiff has or had no right title and possession on the suit land wherein the defendant has been in peaceful, possession, that deeds created by the plaintiff are antedated, and forged and that the suit is liable to be dismissed.

5. That subsequently the suit was transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge Additional Court Rajshahi and was renumbered as OC suit No. 69 of 1990.

6. On 9-3-1991 plaintiff filed an application for amendment of the plaint stating, inter alia, that the defendant has died on 25-11-1990 corresponding to 10th Agrahaiyan 1397 BS and as such, amendment was necessary to strike out the name of the deceased defendant from the plaint and add the names of the legal heirs of the defendant in his place to proceed with the suit. The plaintiff also filed separate application and prayed for taking the case out of the list of peremptory hearing. The prayer for amendment of the plaint was seriously opposed on behalf of the defendant. It was contended that the sole defendant died on 16-2-1990 and since no application for substitution was filed within time limited by law which is 90 days from the date of death of the deceased the suit abated and that belated application for substitution filed in the form of amendment of the plaint is misconceived and not maintainable. Moreover the defendant produced and filed death certificate dated 19-2-1990 issued by Dr SA. Nurul Alam Resident Neuro Surgeon of Rajshahi Medical College Hospital who visited and examined the deceased after his death on 16-2-90. According to death certificate Annexure-A, the defendant died on 16-2-90 due to cardiac respiratory failure. The next date was fixed on 27-1-91 by the learned Court for hearing the application when plaintiff prayed for time and the application was fixed for hearing on 14-2-91. On that date the hearing was again adjourned and fixed on 6-3-91 for filing the death certificate, but no such death certificate was produced before the court till 6-3-1991.

7. The learned Assistant Judge by his order dated 6-3-1991 allowed the application for amendment and ordered to amend the plaint and suit register as prayed for at a cost of Taka 200 only.

8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order the defendant moved this court with an application under section 115 Civil Procedure Code and obtained the present Rule.

9. Mr Asad Hossain Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant petitioner submits that abatement of the suit having taken effect for non substitution of the legal representatives of the deceased sole defendant within prescribed time the trial Court has committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice in allowing the belated application for amendment thereby impleading the legal representative of deceased defendant by way of the amendment of the plaint. Mr Chowdhury further submits that the plaintiff has taken resort to the provision of Order VI of the Code of Civil Procedure only to avoid the effect of abatement of the suit. Mr Asad Chowdhury eloquently argues that provision of the said order regarding amendment of the pleading has no manner of application in the matter of substitution of deceased party in suit.

10. Mr Khandaker Saiful Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite parties, on the other hand, has contended that the learned Assistant Judge has passed the impugned order in exercise of his discretion and has impleaded the name of the legal heirs of the defendant in the interest of Justice which should not be interfered in revision. Mr Khandaker further submits that such amendment has been made to determine the real questions in controversy between the parties and that instead of filing an application for substitution under Order 22 rule 9 Civil Procedure Code an application for amendment has been filed out of mistaken view of law. Mr Khandaker continues to submit that in view of the fact that abatement of the suit precludes fresh suit on the same cause of action and as such, according to him, the learned Assistant Judge committed no illegality in allowing the prayer for amendment in the interest of justice.

11. Mr Huq arduously argues that although the petition filed by the plaintiff is framed as an application for amendment the same is in essence and substance an application for substitution. As such the learned Assistant Judge has committed no wrong in allowing the petition.

12. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff has placed his reliance on a judgment in the case of Maqbul Ahamed and others vs Shoeb Chowdhury and others reported in 44 DLR 156 and another Judgment in the case of Md Matiur Rahman vs Lal Banu Bibi and others reported in 1986 BLD 432.

13. I have heard the learned Advocate at length and perused the application papers annexed and the case laws cited at the Bar.

14. It is pertinent to note that in view of the provision laid down in Order 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the death of several plaintiffs or the sole plaintiff or several defendants or the sole defendant, as the case may be, and right to suit survives, legal representatives of heirs of the deceased party are to be brought on record to proceed with the suit. The application commonly known as application for substitution is to be filed within time limited by law. The prescribed period of limitation for filing an application to have the legal representatives of deceased plaintiff made party and for having legal representatives of deceased defendant in each case is 90 days from the date of death under provisions of Article 176 of the Limitation Act (IX of 1908). Sub-rule (3) of rule 4 of the said order specifically provided that where no application for substitution is made within the time limited by law the suit shall abate as against the deceased defendant. When a suit abates for want of substitution plaintiff may apply for an order to set aside abatement under sub-rule (2) of rule 9 of Order 22. If it is proved that plaintiff was prevented by any sufficient cause from continuing the suit the court shall set aside abatement. In considering prayer for substitution the court has a duty to see whether the application has been filed in time and whether the suit has abated in the meantime for non-substitution. Though the court has wide discretion to allow either party to alter or amend his pleading at any stage of the proceeding for the purpose of determining the real questions in controversy between the parties on consideration of special circumstances of each case under Order 6 rule 17 Civil Procedure Code the same in my view is no application for introduction of the legal representatives of deceased party in the plaint.

<u>15. It is curious to note that plaintiff-opposite party not only failed to product any material to substantiate his claim that defendant died on 25-11-90 but also produced no evidence to repel the contention of the defendant that the sole defendant died on 16-2-90 and the suit had already abated. Whenever particular party dies during pendency of the suit and an application for bringing the legal representatives of the deceased on record is made in that behalf the court has to see that the application has been filed in time with reference to the date of death stated in the petition. In the instant case on the date of death one party contradicts the other in that the date of death according to plaintiff opposite party is 25-11-90 while the date of death is 16-2-90 according to the defendant. The defendant has submitted death certificate dated 19-2-99 issued by the Resident Neuro surgeon of the Rajshahi Medical College Hospital to show that the defendant died on 16-2-90. It may be mentioned that if ninety days is counted from the alleged date of death 16-2-90 application filed is clearly out of time. In that view of the matter the plaintiff-opposite party was allowed time on his prayer to produce death certificate and once again he was also directed by the court to file death certificate to which the plaintiff-opposite party did not respond. Thereafter on 6-3-91 the learned Assistant Judge most illegally and abruptly decided to allow the application and passed the impugned order. Having regard to the specific provisions of law laid down in Order 22 Civil Procedure Code the heirs of deceased party cannot be impleaded by way of amendment of the plaint which is contrary to the provision of Order 22 Civil Procedure Code. If such an action is approved it will render the specific provisions for substitution under Order 22 completely nugatory and redundant. The provisions for amendment of pleading has no bearing in the matter of substitution of legal representative of a deceased party and it is not to be used as subsidiary provision of the Order 22 Civil Procedure Code as a device to overcome the effect of bar of abatement in the suit. The plaintiff ought to have filed proper application praying for recording the legal heirs of the deceased under Order 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure to continue the suit which he did not. In the facts and circumstances of this case since the plaintiff opposite party did not apply for substitution in time according to law in the court below the application filed by the plaintiff opposite party only for striking out the name of the deceased defendant and inducting the names of the legal representatives of the deceased by way of amendment of the plaint quoting alleged death of the defendant on 25-11-90 not supported by any material cannot be considered as a valid and proper application. In fact, such an application being filed on misconception of law is out and out misconceived, not maintainable and must fail on that score. In the above premises, I find no substance in the contention of the learned Advocate of the plaintiff opposite party that the application filed by the plaintiff-opposite party in the court below is in essence and substance an application for substitution. The learned Assistant Judge failed to appreciate the relevant provisions of law and illegally allowed the application for amendment of plaint. The impugned order is ex facie a non-speaking order as no reason has been assigned for passing the order.</u>

16. The facts and circumstances and principles of law applied in the rulings relied upon by the plaintiff-opposite party are distinguishable from those involved in this case and as such, not applicable to the present case.

17. In view of the above the impugned order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, out of misconception of law in a most whimsical and arbitrary manner has occasioned failure of justice and cannot be sustained.

18. This Rule, therefore succeeds, the impugned order dated 6-3-91 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Rajshahi in 402/1982, 69 of 1990 is hereby set aside.

19. In the result the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

The order of stay of further proceedings of OC suit No. 402 of 1982, 69 of 1990 granted by this court at the time of issuing the Rule is hereby vacated.

End.
